default.description: What the main window is permitted to do. Deliberately small: every addition here widens what a compromised frontend could reach, and BibleCompose's frontend renders content that arrived by email. `dialog:allow-open` is the folder picker and nothing else -- not save, not message, not ask -- because choosing a project is the one thing the window needs the filesystem for. Its own commands are granted by name (`allow-…`), because they are declared in build.rs so that the editor windows (capabilities/editor.json) are refused them.

editor.description: What an editor window — easy-usfm, opened on one of the project's books (ADR-007) — is permitted to do. The editor's own shell commands (`easy-usfm:default`), which open only the book the window was opened on and save it through easy-usfm's save ladder; the dialogs Save As, Insert Image and the unsaved-changes guard need; setting its own title and closing itself; and handing a link to the operating system. None of BibleCompose's own commands: an editor renders a book's text and has no reason to start a build, fetch a font or open a project. And not easy-usfm's own update check, which `easy-usfm:default` would grant: BibleCompose updates the editor with itself (ADR-008), and the check is also compiled out of the plugin here, so the deny is the second of two locks.
